newsitem.title: USA: Round-the-world balloonist lands in India.
newsitem.headline: Round-the-world balloonist lands in India.

text.p: American adventurer Steve Fossett landed his balloon in India on Monday, his control headquarters said, ending his attempt to become the first to fly around the world in a balloon nonstop.

Fossett touched down at 2:40 EST (0740 GMT) about 65 miles (105 km) north of Varanasi not long after setting a record for time spent aloft in a balloon, but only about half-way toward his around the world goal. He began his flight late last Monday night in St. Louis.
The command center for the 52-year-old American said it received confirmation of his landing from air traffic control authorities in India.
He was reported to be well and had already received an invitation to dinner from Bengali government officials as well as from the U.S. ambassador to India, his headquarters said.

Fossett was forced to abandon his quest for one of manned flight's oldest goals after he ran short of fuel -- due primarily to a detour he was forced to take around Libya when the government of that country would not let him fly over last Friday. Libya later granted permission but not before Fossett had headed south.
Not long before landing, Fossett broke the record of six days, 16 minutes for time spent in a manned balloon flight. The endurance record was set in 1981 by Americans Ben Abruzzo and Troy Bradley.
